subject: giant petrel seabird
title: A Seabird With a 2-Meter Wingspan Drowns Seal Pups and Kills Penguins

scenes.text: Sailors call this bird the stinker. Penguins have a better reason to fear it.
The giant petrel is the size of a small albatross, with a wingspan over two meters and a bill built for tearing.
It scavenges dead whales and seals, pushing its whole head inside the carcass. Its face comes out stained red. Hence the other name: sea vulture.
But it also hunts. It kills penguin chicks, seabirds up to albatross size, and even adult penguins.
On South Georgia in 2021, scientists filmed petrels picking off fur seal pups left alone on the beach, driving them into the shallows and holding them under until they tired.
Its defence is as nasty: it squirts foul stomach oil at anything that comes too close. Stinker, indeed.

description:
Giant petrels are the largest petrels, about 90 cm long with a wingspan over 2 metres. They are the only petrels that feed on land, scavenging seal and whale carcasses by pushing their heads inside, which stains their faces and earned them the name sea vulture.
They also kill: penguin and albatross chicks, seabirds up to adult albatross size, and adult penguins. In the 2021 breeding season at South Georgia, researchers filmed giant petrels attacking unattended Antarctic fur seal pups, dragging them toward the water and blocking or holding them under until they drowned, reported in the journal Aquatic Mammals in 2022. Adults and chicks defend themselves by squirting foul-smelling stomach oil.
